docs.title: SnakeML
docs.text:
SnakeML is the ML library made in Python and for Python. It runs through the plain Python interpreter, trading speed for simplicity, and provides generalized solutions that you can later shape for yourself.

Python 3.9+ · zero hard dependencies (pytest/mypy optional for dev).

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
SnakeML mostly consists of a few simple types that branch into functional classes:

Type Role Array (structs) Powers tensors and their operations matlib Pure-functional math kernels on nested lists (linalg, broadcasting, reductions, RNG) Layer (basic) Powers forward / backward passes, stores params and input Criterion (basic) Powers losses and gradients Activation(Layer) Powers nonlinear activations Sequential (basic) Powers neural networks Optimizer (basic) Powers gradient descent (SGD, Adam) debug Cross-cutting logging, validation, error hierarchy, operation contexts

This means that YOU can implement your own solutions if you haven't found one in the library. The base is here — the task is up to you.

docs.title: matlib
docs.text:
import matlib
  • broadcasting: broadcast(a, b), elementwise(a, b, op)
  • linalg: matmul matvec outer tensordot transpose permute inverse solve det cross cholesky
  • ops: exp log log2 log10 sqrt square abs sin cos tan asin acos atan atan2 sinh cosh tanh floor ceil round clip sign
  • stats: sum mean variance std max min prod argmax argmin count_nonzero norm and _axis variants with keepdims
  • manipulation: concatenate stack split unbind flip
  • rng: normal(mean=0.0, std=1.0)

docs.title: basic
docs.text:
import basic
  • Layers: Layer · Linear(input_dim, output_dim, initializer) · Conv2D(input_dim, output_dim, kernel, stride) · MaxPool2D (placeholder)
  • Activations: LinearActivation ReLU GELU Sigmoid Tanh Softmax
  • Losses: MSE() · CrossEntropy() (expects softmax probs + one-hot)
  • Optimizers: SGD(layers, lr=0.01) · Adam(layers, lr=0.001, beta1, beta2, epsilon) — pass model.layers
  • Networks: Sequential(layers) — forward/backward only; optimization lives in the optimizer
  • Initializers (functors): Zeros Ones Normal Uniform Constant XavierNormal XavierUniform KaimingNormal KaimingUniform
  • Transformers (experimental): Embedding PosEmbedding LayerNorm Residual Attention
  • from basic.utils import im2col

docs.title: Quick start (dev)
docs.text: This is a walkthrough through the SnakeML codebase, from the bottom layer up. Read it alongside the source — each section points at concrete files.

docs.title: The map
docs.text:
mllib/
├── matlib/        pure math on nested lists (no class dispatch)   ← layer 1
├── structs/       the Array container, composed from mixins      ← layer 2
├── basic/         NN layers, losses, optimizers                  ← layer 3
├── debug/         logging / validation / errors (cross-cutting)
├── localdev/      scratch demo & experiment scripts
└── tests/         pytest + unittest

Dependencies flow one way: basic → structs → matlib, with debug used by all of them.

docs.title: Level 0 — debug/: the nervous system
docs.text:
Small, mostly-independent modules you should read first because everything imports them:

File What it gives debug/config.py Module-level config dict: configure(**overrides), set_level(...), is_enabled(...), env-var config debug/logger.py Custom Logger with debug/info/warning/error/critical; get_logger(name); bind(**ctx) for preset context debug/context.py operation_context(name, **meta) — a context manager that installs ambient metadata ("what op am I in") debug/errors.py LibraryError(root) → ValidationError → ShapeError / TypeMismatchError, OperationError(context, details) debug/validator.py ensure_type(...), ensure_shape(...) — raise the exceptions above debug/formatter.py [snakeML]-prefix formatting, describe(value) — one-line human-readable object dump debug/diagnostics.py JSON-ish runtime snapshots for log lines

The pattern used everywhere in basic/:

from debug.context import operation_context
from debug.errors import OperationError

with operation_context("linear.forward", layer="Linear"):
    try:
        ...           # risky math
    except Exception as e:
        raise OperationError(context=current_context(), details=str(e))

So when something fails deep in the network, the error carries the ambience of where it happened.

docs.title: Level 1 — matlib/: dtype-agnostic math kernels
docs.text:
matlib functions take and return plain nested lists (or Arrays — they unwrap duck-typed data). There is no dispatch class here; it's the functional core.

  • matlib/broadcasting.py — the heart: broadcast(a, b) implements NumPy broadcast semantics (with an extra lenient 1-D-vs-2-D alignment), and elementwise(a, b, op) combines broadcasting with arbitrary binary callables. Every a + b, a * b, comparison etc. on Array funnels through here.
  • matlib/linalg.py — transpose, matmul (batched over leading axes), matvec, outer, tensordot (general axis-contraction — used by Conv2D), inverse (Gauss-Jordan), solve, det, cross, cholesky, permute.
  • matlib/ops.py — unary elementwise kernels: exp, log, sqrt, tanh, clip, ... via the recursive _apply_unary.
  • matlib/stats.py — two tiers: global reductions over flat iterables (sum, mean, variance, ...) and axis-aware versions (sum_axis(arr, axis, keepdims)).
  • matlib/manipulation.py — concatenate, stack, split, unbind, flip.
  • matlib/rng.py — the entire randomness source: normal(mean, std) via Box–Muller on random.random().
  • matlib/operators.py, matlib/reductions.py — reserved placeholder namespaces.
  • matlib/__init__.py — re-exports ~42 names (intentionally shadowing builtins abs/sum/min/max).

Run the tests as you read; they're the executable spec of all this.

docs.title: structs/dtypes.py
docs.text: Not a dtype system — it's the shared type-alias vocabulary used by every signature: Scalar, NestedList, ArrayLike, IndexKey, Shape, Strides, plus a TypeVar-based 3.9-compatible Self fallback (ArrayT/ReturnSelf).

docs.title: structs/array/protocol.py — the contract
docs.text:
class ArrayProtocol(Protocol):
    data: NestedList; shape: Shape; strides: Strides; offset: int; ndim: int
    ...

This is the key design pattern: each behavioral mixin subclasses ArrayProtocol, so mypy type-checks each mixin independently against the shared contract, and Array satisfies it simply by inheriting the mixin composition.

docs.title: structs/array/mixins.py — the composition
docs.text:
class ArrayMixins(ArrayConstructors, ArrayUtilsOps, ArrayShapeOps, ArrayMathOps, ArrayStatsOps):
    pass

ArrayArray (sic: Array in structs/array/array.py) is class Array(ArrayMixins) — a pure shell. Attributes are computed eagerly at construction (_to_list + _get_shape + _strides) and recomputed after every in-place mutation; there are no views yet (offset is reserved for that).

docs.title: The four behavioral mixins
docs.text:
Mixin File Highlights Constructors constructors.py zeros/ones/eye/full/arange/linspace/randn/tile/... — classmethod factories filling per-element over a shape grid Utils utils.py (~875 lines, the big one) internal shape machinery (_to_list, _get_shape, _strides, _wrap_result via type(self)), plus flatten/tolist/item, concatenate/stack/split/unbind, where/take/put/gather/scatter/masked_fill/astype, unique/sort/argsort/searchsorted/shuffle/choice Math ops.py (~910 lines) full dunder surface (+ - * / // % ** & \| ^ abs + r*'s + i*'s), all routed through _elementwise(...) → matlib.broadcasting.elementwise; linalg delegation (dot via tensordot, matmul, outer, inverse, ...); unary delegation to matlib.ops Shape shape.py reshape (single -1 inference), squeeze/unsqueeze, swapaxes/moveaxis/permute/transpose, T, broadcast_to, roll, pad (2-D) Stats stats.py sum/mean/var/std/max/min/prod/argmax/argmin/norm all with (axis=None, keepdims=False)

In-place ops go through _update_self(result), which rebinds data/shape/ndim.

docs.title: structs/array/indexing.py and stats.py
docs.text:
• indexing.py — the NumPy-style indexing engine: _normalize_key validates int / slice / bool list / Array / ..., expands Ellipsis, pads missing trailing keys as full slices; _getitem / _setitem run over it. Slicing is garaunteed by tests like arr[:, 1].
  • stats.py — thin (axis, keepdims) adapters calling matlib.stats.*_axis.

Key things to know before hacking on the Array:

  1. Everything rebuilds via type(self) — subclassing keeps fluent returns.
  2. dtype is an inferred string label on demand (astype casts to native Python types); there is no native-typed backing store.
  3. MRO gotcha: ArrayConstructors.repeat/tile (classmethods) shadow same-named instance methods in ArrayShapeOps — those instances are currently dead code.

docs.title: basic/layers.py — the core abstraction
docs.text:
class Layer:
    params: Dict[str, Any]      # e.g. {"w": Array, "b": Array}
    grads: Dict[str, Any]       # filled by backward, same keys
    submodules: Dict[str, Layer]
    input: Any                  # cached for backward

    def forward(self, input_data): ...
    def backward(self, output_grad): ...     # returns d(input)
    def parameters(self): ...                # recursive, dotted keys

Linear(input_dim, output_dim, initializer=None): - forward: w.matmul(input) + b under operation_context("linear.forward") - backward: grads["w"] = grad.outer(self.input), grads["b"] = grad, returns w.T.matmul(grad)

Conv2D(input_dim, output_dim, kernel, stride) uses basic/utils.im2col (patch extraction via input[:, y:y+KH, x:x+KW] slice tricks) + tensordot over the last three axes. (MaxPool2D is a placeholder.)

docs.title: basic/activations.py
docs.text: All subclasses of Activation(Layer): ReLU, Sigmoid, Tanh, GELU (tanh approx + hand-derived backward), Softmax (max-subtracted for stability; supports 1-D and row-wise 2-D; compact Jacobian backward p*(g - (p*g).sum())), LinearActivation (identity). Convention: forward coerces non-Array inputs and caches self.input/self.output for the derivative.

docs.title: basic/criterions.py
docs.text:
• MSE: forward 0.5*(y_pred-y_true)**2 (elementwise), backward (y_pred - y_true) — the 0.5 cancels the d²/dx².
  • CrossEntropy: assumes pred is already softmax probabilities and targets are one-hot; backward (y_pred - y_true)/N. Heavily instrumented: operation_context, ensure_type, failures become OperationError.

docs.title: basic/optimizers.py
docs.text:
class Optimizer:
    def __init__(self, layers=None, lr=0.01): ...

Pass model.layers. step() walks (dotted_path, params_dict, key, grad) via _recursive_items — so a nested params["w"]["Q"] (as used by Attention) falls out for free — and mutates each leaf in place. SGD is params -= lr * grad; Adam adds bias-corrected moments. zero_grad() sets layer.grads = {}.

docs.title: basic/nn.py
docs.text:
• LayerList(list) registers each layer as submodules["<index>"].
  • Sequential chains forward left-to-right and backward right-to-left — that ordering is the whole backprop mechanism; autograd-style magic isn't needed because each layer's backward is hand-derived.

docs.title: basic/initializers.py & basic/transformers.py
docs.text: Initializers are functors (__call__): Zeros/Ones/Normal/Uniform/Constant/Xavier*/Kaiming*, used by Linear (default XavierNormal); Constant(value, shape) takes the value first. transformers.py has experimental building blocks: Embedding (sparse row-gradient accumulation into grads["w"]), LayerNorm, Residual, single-head Attention (hand-derived backward, nested parameter dict).

docs.title: Level 4 — localdev/ and tests/
docs.text:
localdev/ scripts aren't part of the installed package; each demos one corner:

  • nn_test.py — the canonical end-to-end training loop (the exact loop from Quick start): Sequential([Linear(3,2), ReLU(), Linear(2,1)]) + SGD(model.layers, 0.01) + 1000 iterations.
  • cnn.py — Conv2D forward/backward + one SGD step on a fixed 4×4 input.
  • test_trans.py — Embedding with a hand-built table, a fixed gradient, one optimizer step; inspect e.grads.
  • main.py, temp.py — a single-neuron mini-demo, and an Array featurure tour.

tests/ runs with pytest (files use both unittest classes and pytest style) from the repo root:

python -m pytest tests/ -v        # or: .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/
.venv/bin/python -m mypy          # type checks structs, matlib, debug (per pyproject.toml)

Coverage: test_array.py (indexing, stats, linalg, embedding-optimizer interaction, error cases), test_debug.py (logger, contexts, config gating, validators), test_initializers.py (exact fills + shapes).

docs.title: Suggested reading order
docs.text:
1. debug/errors.py + debug/context.py — 100 lines, the exception/context idiom.
  2. matlib/broadcasting.py — how elementwise math actually works.
  3. structs/array/array.py + protocol.py + mixins.py — the container.
  4. Pick one mixin (ops.py is the most instructive) and the tests of it.
  5. basic/layers.py, then activations.py, criterions.py, optimizers.py, nn.py.
  6. Run localdev/nn_test.py; add a step counter and print layer.grads each iteration — that's the backprop mechanism laid bare.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/yourbrolol/SnakeML.git
cd SnakeML
python -m pip install .

Dependencies: none (pytest for running tests).

docs.title: Train your first model
docs.text:
Everything lives in plain packages — add the repo root to your path (or pip install -e .) and go:

from structs import Array
from basic import Sequential, Linear, ReLU
from basic.criterions import MSE
from basic.optimizers import Adam

# tiny regression problem: y = x0 + x1
X = [
    [0, 0], [0, 1], [1, 0], [1, 1], [2, 3], [4, 1],
]
Y = [[0], [1], [1], [2], [5], [5]]

model = Sequential([Linear(2, 4), ReLU(), Linear(4, 1)])
opt = Adam(model.layers, lr=0.01)
crit = MSE()

for step in range(500):
    opt.zero_grad()
    y_pred = model.forward(X)
    loss = crit.forward(y_pred, Array(Y))
    grad = crit.backward(y_pred, Array(Y))
    model.backward(grad)
    opt.step()

print(model.forward([3, 4]))   # ~ [[7]]

Note

Pass model.layers — not model — to the optimizer. Sequential doesn't implement params/grads; the optimizer reads them off each Layer.

docs.title: What just happened
docs.text:
1. model.forward(X) walks the layers left-to-right.
  2. crit.backward produces the gradient of the loss w.r.t. predictions (e.g. MSE → (y_pred - y_true)).
  3. model.backward(grad) walks the layers right-to-left, filling each layer's grads dict.
  4. opt.step() updates params[key] -= lr * grad (recursively, so nested dicts work too).
  5. opt.zero_grad() clears layer.grads = {} at the top of each iteration.

docs.title: Using the Array
docs.text:
Array behaves like a mini NumPy: NumPy-style indexing, broadcasting arithmetic, reshaping, reductions, linalg:

from structs import Array

a = Array([[1, 2], [3, 4]])
a.shape          # (2, 2)
a[1, 0]          # 3
a[:, 1]          # Array([[2], [4]])
a + a            # elementwise, NumPy-style broadcasting
a.matmul(a)      # batched matrix multiply
a.sum(axis=0)    # Array([4, 6])
a.reshape(-1)    # Array([[1], [2], [3], [4]])
Array.zeros((2, 3))
Array.randn((2, 2))
